Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap - that matches what we discussed. Confirming the following from AcmeFin: 

1) Training opt-out: yes, AcmeFin requires that any customer data (PII and derived features) not be used to update or train any public/shared Redwood models or model-improvement pipelines. We need a written acknowledgement and opt-out in our agreement.

2) Data residency and retention: all production data and logs must be stored in US-only regions. For logs, we prefer retention no longer than 30 days for request/response payloads; audit logs (request metadata, timestamps, request IDs) can be retained up to 12 months for compliance. Please advise if Redwood can support that retention split.

3) Logging controls: we need the ability to disable full request payload logging for a subset of routes that carry sensitive PII fields; we may be able to provide a schema for those routes. Would Rishi on your side be the right person to discuss technical controls (KV cache, prefix caching, log redaction) and how to implement route-level logging policies?

Attached: acmefin-internal-approval.pdf (pdf, 125KB)

Thanks,
Sanjay
Head of Risk & Compliance, AcmeFin
